messages.subject: fPortfolio development ideas
messages.body_plain:
During the first r-metrics meeting in Meielisalp was mentioned that fPortfolio library's target should be on small portfolios (because of optimization problems). I found some very interesting functions in this proprietary library (link to the user manual below) since constraints over number of assets and rebalancing options are most common problems in portfolio management.

Please let me know what you think.
Best regards
Daniele Amberti

http://www.burns-stat.com/pages/Product/pop_use_man.pdf

messages.subject: fImport: Import yahoo income statement
messages.body_plain:
Greetings!

I am envisioning expanding the fImport module, so that quarterly data of companies can be imported into R. Much like the yahooKeystats() command, I would like to import data from http://finance.yahoo.com/q/is?s=IBM.  

I am not familiar with R programming yet, and before starting spending my time in writing the module, I wanted to know if any efforts in this direction have been made in the past. If not I would appreciate any support.

Best regards

Christian

 
--

messages.subject: economagicImport - NAs error
messages.body_plain:
Dear Maintainers,

Using the most recent Windows binary (270.74) I get a large number of 
NAs when importing data from economagic.


The following code ...

oil.prices <- economagicSeries("var/west-texas-crude-long", frequency = 
"monthly", from = "1980-01-01",  to = Sys.timeDate())
plot(oil.prices, main="WTI Spot Prices")


Results in the following message....

Warning message:
In economagicImport(query, file, source, frequency, from, to, nDaysBack,  :
  NAs introduced by coercion


This only started to happen in the last month, so I suspect economagic 
changed how their website expresses data.

Does the current linux source (290.75) have this issue?

If it doesn't, when do you estimate you'll be able to update the Windows 
binary?


Mike Morgan



Michael Morgan

messages.subject: fUtilities::isS4
messages.body_plain:
Hi!
    I'm having some difficulties using the isS4 function in 
the fUtilities package.  Specifically, I think that the 
test for NULL slotNames may not always give the correct 
result.

For example, consider an lm object:

> x = rnorm(10)
> y = rnorm(10)
> z = lm(y~x)
> base::isS4(z)
[1] FALSE
> fUtilities::isS4(z)
[1] TRUE
> slotNames(z)
[1] ".S3Class"

     Since showMethods(class='lm') doesn't return anything, I don't
think lm objects should be identified as S4 objects by isS4.

     Thanks!
                                        - Phil Spector
 					 Statistical Computing Facility
 					 Department of Statistics
 					 UC Berkeley
 					 spector at stat.berkeley.edu

messages.subject: fUtilities::isS4
messages.body_plain:
Yohan, Diethelm,

On 30 January 2009 at 09:17, Yohan Chalabi wrote:
| BTW, have you noticed that the new Rmetrics packages should not
| depend on 'fUtilities' which will be considered as deprecated in the
| future.
| 
| If you are using 'fCalendar' and 'fSeries', please move to their new
| versions named timeDate and timeSeries respectively.

Would it be possible to get more regular updates about what is, or is not, or
will be, or will no longer be, part of what is considered to be Rmetrics ?

Maybe it is just me, but I find it confusing that a project called 'Rmetrics'
once had a package called Rmetrics which it no longer has ... The calendar /
date package transition wasn't all that smooth either. As start, a high-level
changelog and/or roadmap could be added to the wiki.  You may also want to
use this list. And/or the r-packages or r-sig-finance list.

Finally, I personally would also vote for re-instating the Rmetrics package
as it can give you at least a small hook (by looking at the search path, or
at installed.packages(), or ...) into alerting actual users to the fact that
they still have something installed that you now deem deprecated.  Otherwise,
I fear you will be confronted with this problem for a long time indeed.

Just my $0.02.  

Regards, Dirk

-- 
Three out of two people have difficulties with fractions.
